First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{42}{7} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=7$ and $r=6.$ Substituting these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{7(1-{6}^{N})}{1-6} \\  & =\frac{7(1-{6}^{N})}{(-5)} \\  & =-\frac{7}{5}(1-{6}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{7}{5}({6}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
